extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, extramural research scientists, peer reviewers, and NIH review administrators (SRAs, CSR staff, IC staff)
extracted.subtask_short: NIH peer review of grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: High-level description of the NIH initial peer review process and oversight: initial review groups of extramural scientists rate the scientific and technical merit of grant and training applications, with process management by SRAs, CSR, ICs and policy oversight by OER and PROG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific and technical merit
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the initial review is to rate the scientific and technical merit of the proposed research or research training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial review groups are composed of scientists from the extramural research community who evaluate and rate scientific and technical merit. This rating is the principal objective of the initial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial review process management (SRAs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The initial review process is managed by Scientific Review Administrators (SRAs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRAs manage the review process to ensure orderly conduct of the initial peer review; they administer review groups and procedural aspects of initial evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy development and implementation (OER)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Extramural Research (OER) manages the development and implementation of policies and procedures that pertain to peer review conducted in all components of the NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OER provides central policy guidance and procedural standards that govern how peer review is conducted across NIH components to ensure consistency and compliance with overarching rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of applications to review bodies (CSR vs ICs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Center for Scientific Review (CSR) manages the initial review groups that review most investigator-initiated applications; the awarding institutes and centers (ICs) manage the review of applications submitted in response to special solicitations and for unique programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate routing/assignment ensures applications are reviewed by the correct body (CSR for most unsolicited investigator-initiated apps; ICs for program-specific or solicited applications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer expertise appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewer expertise must be appropriate for the needs of science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Peer Review Oversight Group (PROG) advises to ensure reviewer expertise matches scientific needs; matching expertise to applications is a criterion for quality peer review and is monitored by oversight bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review processes keep pace with advances in research
rubrics_metrics.description: Review processes should keep pace with current advances in research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PROG's remit includes advising and recommending changes so that monitoring, coordination, and evaluation of peer review evolve with scientific advances; this implies periodic review and updating of review procedures and criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of public representatives/participants in review
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of Inclusion of Public Representatives/Participants in Scientific Peer Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page identifies inclusion of public representatives as an issue under consideration (link/title present), indicating that participation of non-scientific/public representatives in review is a relevant policy dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of explicit statements of review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH announces explicit statements of review criteria (see 'Rating of Grant Applications - NIH Announces New Explicit Statements of Review Criteria').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page references NIH's effort to provide clear, explicit review criteria for rating grant applications; while the page links to those statements, the presence of explicit criteria is a documented policy direction that applicants and reviewers should follow.
